coder.case: Download https://books.toscrape.com/ and save the 20 book titles and prices on that page to books.csv with header title,price.
coder.output:
import requests
from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
import csv

url = "https://books.toscrape.com/"
response = requests.get(url, timeout=30)

soup = BeautifulSoup(response.text, 'html.parser')

books = []
for item in soup.find_all('li', class_='col-xs-6 col-sm-4 col-md-3 col-lg-3'):
    title = item.h3.a.text.strip()
    price = item.find('p', class_='price_color').text.strip()
    books.append({'title': title, 'price': price})

with open('books.csv', 'w', newline='', encoding='utf-8') as csvfile:
    fieldnames = ['title', 'price']
    writer = csv.DictWriter(csvfile, fieldnames=fieldnames)
    writer.writeheader()
    for book in books:
        writer.writerow(book)

print("Saved books.csv with 20 book titles and prices.")

coder.case: Get the Open-Meteo daily maximum temperature forecast for latitude 18.52, longitude 73.86 for 3 days (https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=18.52&longitude=73.86&daily=temperature_2m_max&forecast_days=3&timezone=auto) and save forecast.csv with header date,max_temp.
coder.output:
import requests
from datetime import datetime

url = "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=18.52&longitude=73.86&daily=temperature_2m_max&forecast_days=3&timezone=auto"
response = requests.get(url, timeout=30)

if response.status_code == 200:
    data = response.json()
    daily_data = data['daily']
    dates = [datetime.fromisoformat(date).strftime('%Y-%m-%d') for date in daily_data['time']]
    max_temps = daily_data['temperature_2m_max']

    with open('forecast.csv', 'w') as file:
        file.write('date,max_temp\n')
        for date, temp in zip(dates, max_temps):
            file.write(f'{date},{temp}\n')

    print("Saved forecast.csv with header date,max_temp.")
else:
    print(f"Failed to retrieve data. Status code: {response.status_code}")

import re
from collections import Counter

# Read the text from text.txt
with open('text.txt', 'r') as file:
    text = file.read().lower()

# Extract words using regex
words = re.findall(r'\b\w+\b', text)

# Count the frequency of each word
word_count = Counter(words)
